stem.text: The pumping action of the heart creates hydrostatic pressure in the blood. The table shows the hydrostatic pressure in a blood capillary.
About 90% of the tissue fluid which surrounds a capillary is returned to the blood at the venule end.

A.text: The capillary wall is more permeable at the arteriole end than the venule end.

B.text: The hydrostatic pressure in tissue fluid is higher than in blood.

C.text: There is a higher concentration of dissolved solutes in tissue fluid than in blood.

D.text: There is osmotic movement of water from the tissue fluid into the blood.
